ABSENCE: no test where `missing == []` and a `budget-cap-shed` finding alone makes the retry eligible and re-runs the shed criterion
blocking.finding: No test exercises an ELIGIBLE `--retry` resume whose sole retryable-missing trigger is a budget-shed criterion (no `failed`/`cancelled` journal unit). Every eligible-resume test is seeded via `_indeterminate_with_failed_unit`, which always produces a `failed` unit; the only budget-cap-shed reference in the suite removes shed findings to force a REFUSAL. The `_shed_criteria` enumeration and the shed-only admittance branch (`if not missing and not _shed_criteria(payload)`) are documented as a first-class eligibility path but are never driven green, so a regression there is invisible.
scenarios: A review lands INDETERMINATE purely because the budget cap shed a criterion (no chunk failed); `--retry` should resume and re-run the shed criterion under a fresh budget
A regression that mis-reads the shed-finding reason marker or criteria key would refuse a legitimately-retryable shed-only review, or (inverted) admit an ineligible one
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test that seeds an INDETERMINATE with a budget-shed criterion but no failed unit (e.g. tighten the budget so a criterion sheds while others succeed, with the fake never raising), then assert `review_plan(..., retry=True)` is eligible (not `retry_refused`), issues exactly the shed criterion's finder call, and records `coverage.retry is True`.

evidence: retry.py docstring: 'It layers ONLY two things over the existing chunk-checkpoint resume seam ... a latest-review ELIGIBILITY gate and a fresh attempt budget'
`produce_plan_review_verdict(ctx, ...)` (line 667) receives no journal/digest set — resume is implicit via `sizing.load_checkpoint(ctx, digest)` recomputed in pass1.py:327-337
ABSENCE: no check after the review that `coverage.checkpoint.chunks_resumed > 0` on the retry path, so a retry that reused nothing is indistinguishable from one that reused everything
dropped.finding: The eligible `--retry` resume relies entirely on Pass-1 re-deriving the SAME checkpoint digests it recorded, but nothing threads the journal's recorded digests into `produce_plan_review_verdict`; if the recomputed digest identity diverges from the journal (material/code_ref/topology/extra-context), Pass-1 silently re-runs every unit at full model cost while still being reported as a successful retry. The eligibility gate validates checkpoints load at gate time but there is no post-run assertion that the resume actually reused them.
scenarios: A retry whose digest identity drifts (topology/extra-context recomputation) re-runs all units at full cost but still reports as a normal successful retry with a lineage bump

dropped.finding: On the eligible `--retry` path, the `remediation` and `drift_floor` decisions (lines 650-651) are NOT gated by `not retry`, unlike the reuse short-circuits and drift-refresh directly above/below them which all gained `and not retry`. As a result a resumed retry review still computes remediation/drift eligibility and applies the Pass-3 rising/drift floors, which can narrow (drop findings from) the resumed verdict — a behavior difference from the units' original review that is not called out in the docstring or the docs and may be unintended.
scenarios: A retry resume of an INDETERMINATE where remediation/drift mode is enabled applies a rising/drift floor and silently drops findings that were present in the units being reused
